record.paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can mapping repair and adaptation for knowledge translation be performed when source or target knowledge bases change over time, so that mappings remain valid or consistent without regenerating them from scratch and while preserving as much of the original mapping semantics and query-answering capability as possible?

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, to the best of our knowledge, there is not yet any work in this area for settings which involve source and target KBs.
It is important to see how various repair notions proposed in the literature can be used in the context of knowledge translation and to facilitate the mapping adaptation.

artifact.status_search_result: Existing literature addresses mapping adaptation under evolving schemas (e.g., the ToMAS system) and ontology mapping repair, but no work directly addresses repair and adaptation in the combined source–target knowledge-base translation setting with TBoxes/ABoxes on both sides. Recent surveys and related systems (Kensho, generative translation methods) focus on mapping generation rather than incremental repair under evolution, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Mapping Adaptation under Evolving Schemas
status_evidence.snippet: In dynamic environments like the Web where data sources may change not only their data but also their schemas and semantics, mapping adaptation becomes necessary... The Toronto Mapping Adaptation System (ToMAS) automatically maintains the consistency of mappings as schemas evolve.
status_evidence.claim: Mapping adaptation under schema evolution is studied for data integration but not in the source–target KB translation setting with ontologies.

status_evidence.title: Knowledge translation
status_evidence.snippet: Kensho is a tool for generating mapping rules between two Knowledge Bases (KBs)... Mapping rules are generated by interpreting the correspondences... expressed using SPARQL queries for direct knowledge exchange.
status_evidence.claim: Current knowledge-translation tools focus on generating mappings, not on repairing them under KB evolution.
